definition: Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths from one source in a graph with non-negative edge weights. It grows a set of settled vertices, always settling next the unsettled vertex with the smallest known distance, which a priority queue can supply. A negative edge can make a settled distance wrong, so the algorithm does not allow them.

complexity.time: O((V + E) log V) with a binary heap.
complexity.space: O(V) for distances and the queue.

examples: Driving directions on roads with non-negative lengths
Least-cost routing when no link has a negative cost
